venue.name: Port Hardy Museum & Archives
venue.description: The Port Hardy Museum & Archives is a community museum, archive and gift shop run by the Port Hardy Heritage Society, on Kwakiutl territory at the northern tip of Vancouver Island. Permanent exhibits cover Indigenous history and culture, fishing, mining, logging and local natural history, and include a replica pioneer cabin furnished with home life artifacts. Admission is by donation and the museum is open Tuesday to Saturday, closing between noon and one. The Heritage Society also runs the Port Hardy Visitor Information Centre at 7250 Market Street, which is a different building from the museum.
venue.address: 7110 Market St, Port Hardy, BC V0N 2P0

facility_notes.wheelchair_accessible: Call ahead for additional accessibility needs. We want to ensure visitors can enjoy their trip to the museum.

programs.name: School group tour
programs.description: The museum says it is currently booking school groups and tours, and that it is happy to work with educators to tailor a tour to the class's history curriculum and grade level. Booking is by email to info@porthardymuseum.com, and they ask you to send the students' ages and how many plan to attend because the museum is a small space. Admission to the museum is by donation, and no separate school or group price is published. The museum is closed for January.
programs.what_children_do: Walk through a small museum looking at displays on Indigenous history and culture, fishing, mining, logging, and a small natural history display with shellfish, sea stars, ravens and owls. Step inside a replica pioneer cabin furnished with tools, furnishings and household items from Port Hardy's early days. Staff shape what the tour covers around the class's history topic and grade.
programs.our_note: The museum shuts between noon and one, so a morning visit has to be finished by twelve. They want your children's ages and a head count before they confirm, because it is a small space and they need to know a group will fit. Nothing about cost, group size or how much notice they need is on the site, so ask all three in your first email.
programs.practical_summary: Washrooms are gender neutral, parking is free and the museum is wheelchair accessible, and staff ask you to call ahead about any other access needs. Admission is by donation, and no group price, group size limit, lunch space or bus parking is stated anywhere, so it is worth settling those by email before you book.
programs.evidence: We are currently booking school groups and tours.

gaps: no price for a school or group tour is published; admission to the museum is by donation, which is not the same as free, and the site never says what a group is expected to give
no youngest age or minimum age is published; the museum asks educators to send the students' ages but states no range of its own
no grade range is published either, so whether preschool and daycare groups are taken is unknown
no group size limit is published; the site says only 'We are a small space and want to ensure we can accommodate your group!'
no lead time or minimum notice for booking a school group is published
the site does not say whether school tours can only be booked inside the Tuesday to Saturday opening hours, so days offered is unknown
months offered is unknown; the only seasonal fact published is that the museum is closed for January
no indoor lunch space or eating area is mentioned anywhere on the site
the site says 'Free Parking' but never says whether a school bus can park, so bus parking is left unanswered
no chaperone ratio or number of free adults is published
no cancellation or payment terms are published

the home page and the Visit page give the weekly hours without mentioning the January closure, which is stated on the About and Contact Us pages; the January closure is recorded because it is the more specific statement
